Préambule: Reprise après interruption. L’état est dans la branche. Commence par établir ce qui est fait et ce qui reste par question (Q1 à Q28), sans refaire ce qui est fait.
Voici le prompt original:
```

<pasted_content id="c845">
Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.
</pasted_content id="c845">

```

A post-commit hook can make `git commit` exceed 2 minutes: give it a long timeout. The axiom rule ({propext, Quot.sound} only) forbids core lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (`List.getElem?_mapIdx`, `List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem`, `List.nodup_range`, `List.pairwise_lt_range`): sweep `#print axioms` over every theorem and replace them with local lemmas. Mathlib tactics (`set`, `tauto`) are unavailable. Reviews keep catching report errors: quote old forms from the old commit, count declarations with a command, and base an evidence claim only on a check that would fail on the defect. After fixing review findings, run a second targeted review of the fixes: in MM-03 pass 2 a fix over-rejected legitimate programs. Before calling a clause "missing" from an arbitrage, re-read every earlier arbitrage still in force: in pass 3 the clause needed for exitFrame_no_dangling was A4's root-holder rule, which A1 puts in WF3 and pass 2 had left out. `timeout` does not exist on this Mac: run `lake build` directly (about 2.5 min). When an arbitrage enlarges a definition used in hypotheses (pass 4: `Inv3` gained `NoDangling`), theorems whose text is unchanged silently narrow: give them only the conjunct they use. Before retiring a counterexample whose witness breaks a new invariant clause, look for another witness: pass-4 review found one and flagged the weakening as major. Check obligations against the initial state: the base frame of `S3.init` owns no place, so an obligation about it can be vacuous on reached states. A review fix can itself pick a semantic reading (pass 5: the kind conjunct of `IsInternalFor` rejected a `newArena` that D3 leaves undecided): check every fix for verdicts it changes on cases the text is silent on. Module docstrings must cite the report's own numbering, not the review's decision numbers. Arbiter-supplied theorems can be false: check them on small reached states (owned storage, a parameter that is the ancestor of another) before trying a proof. Every factual claim in the report needs a module witness, or reviewers flag it; never say "blocked until X" without checking escape sequences such as ending the owner value. When a precondition gains clauses, lemmas taking it as a hypothesis narrow silently: name the old precondition (pass 7: `EnterPreBase`) and give the lemmas only what they use. A guard on one operation (G2 on `store`) is usually bypassable through another (a helper authority then `release`/`endUse`/`free`/exit): look for such bypasses before claiming a configuration is excluded. A new check on an operation with a defined failure (`issue` → `fail`) must not turn that failure into `reject`. Use one adversarial reviewer per arbitrage lens; each found distinct real issues in pass 7. When a restriction rejects an old counterexample, try to rebuild a witness that satisfies the new clause before restating it as a rejection (pass 8: a same-shape destination restored `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`). Drop hypotheses a proof does not use. When cases disappear because their state is no longer reached, replay their verdicts on a new reachable state and list the drops. Machine-check every changed verdict the report lists, including the old witnesses' rejected steps. Never state "only clause X fails" as `X → Pre` next to `¬ X`: that is vacuous; name the other clauses (pass 8: `TransferPreBase` with an iff) and state them. Run a second targeted check after fixing verification findings: in pass 8 it caught that vacuous form. `omega` proving a conjunction goal pulls `Classical.choice`: split the goal first. `meta` is a keyword in this Lean: never name a hypothesis `meta`. `set` (Mathlib) is unavailable: use `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x = e := ⟨_, rfl⟩`. `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`ite_cond_eq_true` are deprecated: use `simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]`. When `S3.Usable.mono` is applied with `rfl` for `hP`, give `(s := …) (s' := …)` explicitly or it unifies the wrong way. Simulation theorems: never quantify obligations over all translations (vacuous); put them as per-step premises of the run with parameters fixed once, and give a concrete multi-step run as witness. A universal encoding obligation (`∀ addr, decode (enc addr) = addr`) is unsatisfiable by a finite computable decode: state it per value. `lake env lean` uses the last built olean: rebuild the module before a scratch file uses new declarations. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names. A runner's fallback state must be unreachable (e.g. no frame) or a statement "the run's state is reached" is vacuous when the run fails; give a lemma deriving success from reachability. Projecting `.2` out of an existential passes the elaborator but fails in the kernel: use `obtain`. When `step_ok_of`-style lemmas time out at `whnf`, pass the contract `k` and statics explicitly. Jalon 3 took four check rounds (11/9/9/4 confirmed): each round's fixes need their own narrow check. The list `Sublist` notation `<+` is scoped: write `List.Sublist`; `List.take_add` pulls `Classical.choice`. `omit … in` goes before the docstring. A `def` in a `variable (k : K)` section takes `k` only if it uses it: check call sites. In a multi-line `{ st with … }`, put each field on its own line at one column. Theorems stated for registered arenas (`ar ∈ s.arenas`) do not carry over to library instances: never cite them for one. Before writing "the only effect of X is Y", look for a witness in the other direction (derivability: the missing guard also turned a `fail` into an `ok`).

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

/-! ## Initialization history (§59) -/

/-- Operation `op` writes leaf `l` from state `s` (§59): `write3` or `writeShared` of a list
containing `l`, `store` into `l`, or a `transfer` of which `l` is a destination leaf
corresponding to a source leaf `Init` before the step. -/
def KernelOp.Writes (s : S3) (l : Nat) : KernelOp → Prop
  | .write _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .writeShared _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .store _ p => l = p
  | .transfer src dst => l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∧
      ∃ l' ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l' = some l ∧ s.I l' = .init
authority (no origin) whose footprint is the footprint of a root place containing that leaf. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
place. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/

/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/
structure WF3 (s : S3) : Prop where
  /-- §49.1: the stack is nonempty and duplicate-free, every frame below `nF`. -/

/-- `I2` (§51): the origin of a derived authority exists; the derived mode does not exceed the
origin's, the derived footprint is within the origin's, and the origin of an active derived
authority is valid, that is, active. -/
def I2 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
    ∃ x : Authority, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ y.mode.le x.mode ∧ (∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint) ∧
      (y.active = true → x.active = true)

/-- `I3` (§52): every anchor of a usable place is valid (active). -/
def I3 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- `I4` (§53, first sentence): no read of a region containing a `Moved` leaf is permitted. -/
def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (l : Nat), l ∈ ls → s.I l = .moved →
  ¬ Read3Pre s a ls

/-- `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4` (§57). -/
def Inv3base (s : S3) : Prop := I1 s ∧ I2 s ∧ I3 s ∧ I4 s

/-- `NoDangling` (§54): no active authority covers a leaf of an unusable place. -/
def NoDangling (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
    ∀ q, ¬ s.Usable q → ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∉ y.footprint

/-- `Inv3 = I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling` (§57). -/
def Inv3 (s : S3) : Prop := Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ NoDangling s

/-- `I5` (§57): every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning
obligation, §74), belongs to a usable place. The quantifier ranges over the leaves of the state
(§40): `K.Pinned` on an index that is not a leaf of `s` is not constrained. A specialized
obligation of `K.Pinned`, not a conjunct of the main invariant (§57). -/
def I5 (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ l, l < s.P.length → isLeaf s.P l → (k.Pinned l ∨ s.pin l = true) →
    ∃ q, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-! ## `NoOrphan` (§54) -/

/-- One link of a `NoOrphan` chain (§54): `a` is active and structurally covers every leaf of the
place holding `b`. -/
def CoversHolder (s : S3) (a b : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun z => match z.holder with
    | .place q => s.Active a ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ s.afp a
    | .frame _ => False) False

/-- Consecutive elements of a list are related by `R` (§54, chains of `NoOrphan`). -/
def Linked (R : Nat → Nat → Prop) : List Nat → Prop
  | a :: b :: c => R a b ∧ Linked R (b :: c)
  | _ => True

/-- `NoOrphan` (§54): every active authority held by a place ends a finite, non-repeating chain of
authorities whose first link is active and held by a frame of the stack, each link covering the
whole place holding the next. -/
def NoOrphan (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
    ∃ (a₀ : Nat) (z : Authority) (f : Nat) (c : List Nat), s.A[a₀]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧
      z.holder = .frame f ∧ f ∈ s.F ∧ (a₀ :: c).Nodup ∧ (a₀ :: c).getLast? = some x ∧
      Linked (CoversHolder s) (a₀ :: c)

/-! ## Initial state (§47) -/

/-- Declared static storage (§47): each element is (parent, owning static, kind) with its
initial state, `true` for `Init` and `false` for `Uninit` (read on leaves only). -/
abbrev Statics := List ((Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool)

/-- Well-formed statics declaration (§47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; §49, last
paragraph: the ordering of identifiers represents this well-foundedness, and that of structural
parents): parents and owning statics are earlier statics, and a part has its parent's owning
static (§49.2). -/
def StaticsOK (statics : Statics) : Prop := ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1))

/-- Decidability of `StaticsOK` (§47). -/

/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1, HP5-3, HP5-6) -/

/-- The effect of an accepted `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.5, HP5-1): the pool exists with the
administration right, the handle is valid, and the content conditions hold; the arrival state is
`freeSlotEff`, whose kernel state and resolutions are those of the departure state (no end-of-use
effect; §36, §58), and whose slot is free with its generation incremented. -/
theorem freeSlot_effect {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hst : FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok L')) :
    ∃ pl sl, L.pools[j]? = some pl ∧ pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl ∧ AdminRight L.kern pl ∧
      HandleOK L.kern pl h ∧ FreeContentOK L pl sl.place ∧ L' = freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl ∧
      L'.kern = L.kern ∧ L'.res = L.res ∧
      L'.pools[j]? = some (setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) := by
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl sl hp hH hR hsl hc =>
    exact ⟨pl, sl, hp, hsl, hR, hH, hc, rfl, rfl, rfl, getElem?_set_eq' hp⟩

/-- After an accepted `freeSlot(h)`, the freed slot is free with generation `h.gen + 1`, and `h` is
stale: `resolve` of `h`, and `resolveMany` of any batch containing `h`, fail (HandlePool v0.5,
HP5-6; §89). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_then_stale {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle}
    (hst : FreeSlotStep j h L (.ok L')) :
    (∃ pl' sl', L'.pools[j]? = some pl' ∧ pl'.slots[h.slot]? = some sl' ∧ sl'.live = false ∧
      sl'.gen = h.gen + 1) ∧
    (∀ m o, ResolveStep j h m L' o → o = .fail) ∧
    (∀ hs m o, h ∈ hs → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L' o → o = .fail) := by
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl sl hp hH _ hsl _ =>
    have hp' := getElem?_set_eq' (x := setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) hp
    have hs' := getElem?_set_eq' (x := (⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩ : Slot)) hsl
    have hn : ¬ HandleOK (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl).kern
        (setSlot pl h.slot ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) h := not_handleOK_free hs' rfl
    obtain ⟨-, -, ho⟩ := hH
    rw [hsl] at ho
    exact ⟨⟨_, _, hp', hs', rfl, by rw [ho.1]⟩, fun m => (pool_resolve_invalid_fails hp' hn).2,

/-- A write that sets only `Init` leaves is the identity on the kernel state (§67 effect, §41). -/
theorem write3Eff_of_init {s : S3} {ls : List Nat} (h : ∀ l ∈ ls, s.I l = .init) :
    write3Eff s ls = s := by
  have e : (fun p => if p ∈ ls then InitSt.init else s.I p) = s.I :=
    funext fun p => by
      by_cases hp : p ∈ ls
      · simp only [hp, ↓reduceIte]; exact (h p hp).symm
      · simp only [hp, ↓reduceIte]
  unfold write3Eff; rw [e]

/-- HandlePool v0.5, HP5-3 (mandatory proof (2) of arbitration Q3): the metadata update of
`freeSlot` (free state, generation) is realizable by an authorized write under the administration
right. On every library-reachable state, under `DDSound` (§80) and `StaticsOK` (§47), for every
pool with `AdminRight` (§36), the pool value `v` (the place holding `internal`) exists and the
kernel `write` (§67) of the leaves of `v` through the authority grounding `MetaRight` is accepted;
when the leaves of `v` are `Init`, its effect is the identity on the kernel state. §76.5 requires
`Init` leaves only when the pool is created: on a library-reachable state with `AdminRight`, a leaf
of `v` can be `Moved` (`Witness.meta_write_not_identity`), and the write then changes the kernel
state, while `freeSlot` leaves it unchanged (`freeSlot_effect`). -/
theorem freeSlot_meta_write {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) {L : PState} (hr : PReach k statics L) {pl : Pool}
    (hR : AdminRight L.kern pl) :
    ∃ v a, Arena.arenaValue L.kern pl.entry = some v ∧
      Write3Step a (footprint L.kern.P v) L.kern (.ok (write3Eff L.kern (footprint L.kern.P v))) ∧
      ((∀ l ∈ footprint L.kern.P v, L.kern.I l = .init) →
        write3Eff L.kern (footprint L.kern.P v) = L.kern) := by
  have hk := kernel_guarantee hdd hst L hr
  obtain ⟨⟨y, hy, ya⟩, hm⟩ := hR
  unfold Arena.MetaRight at hm
  cases hv : Arena.arenaValue L.kern pl.entry with
  | none => rw [hv] at hm; exact (hm : False).elim
  | some v =>
    rw [hv] at hm
    obtain ⟨a, -, hex, hall⟩ : HasRight L.kern .modify v := hm
    have hhold : y.holder = .place v := by
      simp only [Arena.arenaValue, Pool.entry, hy] at hv
      revert hv; cases y.holder <;> simp
    have hu : L.kern.Usable v := by
      have := hk.1.holders _ y hy ya; rw [hhold] at this; exact this
    exact ⟨v, a, rfl, Guarded.ok (write_of_right hk hu hex hall fun _ h => h), write3Eff_of_init⟩

    ∃ pl i sl, L.pools[j]? = some pl ∧ AdminRight L.kern pl ∧ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst ∧

      L'.kern.I dst = .init ∧ (∀ l, l ≠ dst → L'.kern.I l = L.kern.I l) ∧
      L'.pools[j]? = some (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) ∧
      slotHandle pl i = some ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩ := by

    refine ⟨pl, i, sl, hp, hst.right, hst, hsl, hf, rfl,
      by show (write3Eff L.kern [dst]).I dst = .init; simp [write3Eff], fun l hl => ?_,
      getElem?_set_eq' hp, by simp [slotHandle, hsl]⟩
    show (write3Eff L.kern [dst]).I l = L.kern.I l
    simp [write3Eff, hl]

(`Access.reachable_kinv`) and `ArenaInv` of the entry (`lReach_inv`) hold there; by I3 the check
of §78.3 never rejects after an accepted `derive` (`resetNoDeps_of_derive`), so the derived
operation is the kernel sequence `derive` then `release` (`reset_iff_derive_release`). -/

/-!
# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v2, non-normative)

A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. The spec does not define
its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
contract **DS-v2**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v2 item
says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
administrations) and §58 (outcomes).

DS-v2 is DS-v1 with six changes. DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark
identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign
mark, rejects if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise
returns those cells to available and removes `m` and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the
derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its static checks, the availability `fail`, then
`split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow` is in place only (same base, extension into
the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise). DS2-1: `mark` requires the administrative
right of §36 (`AdminRight`), else `reject`. DS2-2: `grow` stores the new block authority into the
place that currently holds the block authority `b`. DS2-3: a dead stack (`internal` inactive)
invalidates its marks, so `rewind` of a mark of a dead stack is `fail`, checked with the dead or
foreign mark, before the right. DS2-4: "a cell above m" is every cell at a position `≥ m.top`.
DS2-5: `grow` with `extra = 0` is accepted, an in-place reissue of the same region. DS2-6: `rewind`
on a stack index that does not exist is `fail`, like an invalid mark (`mark`, `push` and `grow` on
a missing stack stay `reject`). Also part of DS-v2: `push` without room is `fail`; `grow` of a `b`
that is no block of the stack is `reject`; §76.5 applies to `newStack`; the dead or foreign mark is
checked before the right of §36; §36 applies to `rewind`.

Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).

/-- Dynamic pinning depends only on the obligations (§74). -/
theorem S3.pin_congr {s s' : S3} (h : s'.pins = s.pins) : s'.pin = s.pin := by
  funext l; simp only [S3.pin, h]

/-- After `pin p`, a leaf is pinned when it was, or when it is a leaf of `p` (§74 `ok`
effect). -/
theorem pin_pinEff (s : S3) (p l : Nat) :
    (pinEff s p).pin l = (s.pin l || decide (l ∈ footprint s.P p)) := by
  simp [S3.pin, pinEff]

/-- Element `j` of `l.modify i f` (§75 `ok` effect), proved without classical reasoning. -/
private theorem getElem?_modify' {α : Type} (f : α → α) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (i j : Nat), (l.modify i f)[j]? = if i = j then (l[j]?).map f else l[j]?
  | [], i, j => by rw [List.modify_nil]; split <;> rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, _ + 1 => by rw [List.modify_zero_cons]; split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)
  | _ :: _, _ + 1, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: l, i + 1, j + 1 => by
    rw [List.modify_succ_cons, List.getElem?_cons_succ, List.getElem?_cons_succ,
      getElem?_modify' f l i j]
    split <;> split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)

/-- The obligations after `unpin o`: obligation `o` is inactive, the others are unchanged (§75
`ok` effect). -/
theorem pins_unpinEff (s : S3) (o i : Nat) :
    (unpinEff s o).pins[i]? =
      if o = i then (s.pins[i]?).map fun ob => { ob with active := false } else s.pins[i]? :=
  getElem?_modify' _ s.pins o i

/-- After `unpin o`, a leaf is pinned exactly when an active obligation other than `o` covers it
(§75 `ok` effect: a leaf stays pinned while another active obligation covers it). -/
theorem pin_unpinEff_iff {s : S3} {o l : Nat} :
    (unpinEff s o).pin l = true ↔
      ∃ (i : Nat) (ob : PinOb), i ≠ o ∧ s.pins[i]? = some ob ∧ ob.active = true ∧
        l ∈ ob.leaves := by
  rw [S3.pin_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, ob, hi, ha, hl⟩
    rw [pins_unpinEff] at hi
    split at hi
    · cases h : s.pins[i]? with
      | none => rw [h] at hi; cases hi
      | some ob' => rw [h] at hi; cases hi; cases ha
    · exact ⟨i, ob, Ne.symm ‹_›, hi, ha, hl⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, ob, hne, hi, ha, hl⟩
    refine ⟨i, ob, ?_, ha, hl⟩
    rw [pins_unpinEff]; split

## HandlePool v0.5 = HandlePool v0.4 annex (Annex D of `~/Downloads/ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`, lines 687–725) with these changes

- HP5-1 `freeSlot` (Q3). Preconditions: administration right (`AdminRight`: live pool, `MetaRight` =
  `Modify` exercisable on the pool value, §36); valid handle; no leaf of the entry is `Init` (each is
  `Uninit` or `Moved`); no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. Effect: the slot
  becomes free and its generation is incremented; NO end-of-use effect: the kernel state is unchanged.
  Outcome order: keep the existing order of `FreeSlotStep` (`reject` without pool or right, then `fail`
  on an invalid handle, then `reject` on the content conditions); Q5 concerns resolution (§89) and is
  not extended to `freeSlot` (report this as a point for the user).
  Remove what only served the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `Exempt`, `DyingAccessOK`, `ContentAnchorOK`,
  `ContentEndPre`, `contentEnd_*`, `freeSlot_preserves*` on `endUseEff`, `freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`

  authority (kernel `write`), `transfer` of the entry's value to a local of the same shape, `unresolve`,

  storage root and stored in the pool value). The transfer relies on the v0.1 §63.4 exemption (the
  entry, the companion, `internal` and its origins ground the right). "Local": prefer a place created
  by `enterFrame` (§72) owned by the current frame; if that is infeasible in the run, use a static
  `Uninit` place directly owned by frame 0 and say why in the docstring and report.
- HP5-3 Mandatory proof (2) (Q3): the metadata update of `freeSlot` (free state, generation) is
  realizable by an authorized write under the administration right: for every library-reachable state
  and pool with `AdminRight`, the kernel `write` (§67, `Write3Pre`) of the leaves of the pool value
  (the place holding `internal`) is accepted. If the effect of that write is the identity on the
  kernel state (the pool value's leaves are `Init`, §76.5), state it too.

## DataStack DS-v2 = DS-v1 with these changes

DS-v1 (brief): "Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from
internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every
mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into

rule), §63.9 (Q1), §71.2 (Q24), §74 and §75 (B#45), §76.6 (Q2), §78.3 (Q7), §82.2 (Q18), §86 (Q6).

**HandlePool v0.5** = HandlePool v0.4 annex D with:
- HP5-1 (Q3): `freeSlot` marks the entry free and increments its generation; no `endUse` effect, the kernel
  state is unchanged. Preconditions: administration right (live pool, `MetaRight`, §36), valid handle, no leaf
  of the entry `Init`.
- HP5-1' (Q3, second follow-up): no active strict descendant of this pool's `internal` covers the entry
  (replaces "derived from a companion"; covers §73 reanchoring onto `internal`). A pool nested in an entry
  blocks freeing that entry; the parent pool's authorities do not block the nested pool's `freeSlot`.

  stale); then `reject` without the right; then `reject` on the content condition.

- HP5-4 (Q4): D.2, D.3 and D.4 (3) per pool (the slot's pool); nested pools allowed.
- HP5-5 (Q5): handle validation precedes the right check in `resolve` and `resolveMany`: `fail`.
- HP5-6 (Q12): a handle of a free entry is stale: `fail`.
- HP5-7 (Q4): every library step is, on the kernel side, a sequence of accepted kernel steps O1–O16; the
  kernel guarantees hold on the whole state (`kernel_guarantee`).

**DS-v2** = DS-v1 with:
- DS2-1 (Q11 d): `mark` requires `AdminRight`, else `reject`.

J'ai ouvert la PR : [ernlang/ern#2](https://github.com/ernlang/ern/pull/2). La condition du brief est remplie : toutes les obligations sont prouvées et il ne reste aucun écart entre verdict attendu et verdict obtenu.

## État par question

La session précédente s'était arrêtée pendant l'audit final, avant la PR. Presque tout était déjà fait ; voici ce que j'ai vérifié dans le code.

| Q | État | Où |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | fait | §63.9 (`dstUsableAfter`) ; `reachable_kinv` sous `DDSound` et `StaticsOK` seuls ; le cycle de la v0 est rejeté (`reachable_cycle_rejected`) |
| Q2 | fait | §76.6 mixte, sur l'état d'arrivée ; porté par `NewArenaBase` |
| Q3 | fait | freeSlot v0.5 ; preuve (1) `freeSlot_after_transfer`, avec `internal` dérivé et un local créé par `enterFrame` ; preuve (2) `freeSlot_meta_write` |
| Q4, Q5, Q12 | fait | garanties par pool ; `fail` avant le contrôle du droit, aussi pour freeSlot ; handle d'une entrée libre périmé : `fail` |
| Q6, Q8, Q13–Q16, Q18, Q24 | fait | spec v0.1 et définitions qui citent ces clauses |
| Q7 | fait | `resetNoDeps_of_noCover` (§78.2 et I3) et `reset_iff_derive_release` (équivalence dans les deux sens) |
| Q9/Q26 | fait | I2 « origine active », §60.1, règle unifiée d'endUse et de free (`keptDesc`) |
| Q10, Q17, Q25, Q27 | fait | lectures retenues ; Q17 remplacée par l'exemption de la suite de Q3 |
| Q11, Q28 | fait | DS-v2 (DS2-1 à DS2-6) |
| Q19–Q22 | fait | jumeau H31a ; cas classés ; tableau des verdicts dans la PR ; `exitRoots` retenu |
| Q23 | **complété dans cette session** | B#45 n'avait aucun témoin sur un état atteignable. J'ai ajouté le cas `Corpus.MM3H.B45` (`d7cb2b7`) : pin(S), pin(f1), unpin de f1, puis transfer(f1, d). Le transfer est rejeté ; le jumeau sans pin(S) est accepté. |

## Vérifications refaites

- `lake build` : 28 jobs, aucun avertissement.
- Le grep des tokens interdits ne trouve rien.
- `collectAxioms` sur les 25 modules (6396 constantes) : rien en dehors de `propext` et `Quot.sound`.

## Points ouverts, listés dans la PR, non bloquants

1. **Spec v0.1** : la phrase de la v0 « This edition has been validated… » a été recopiée telle quelle et contredit l'en-tête. Elle n'est pas dans la liste des amendements, donc je ne l'ai pas modifiée.
2. **Preuve (2) de Q3** : si une feuille de la valeur du pool est `Moved`, l'écriture qui réalise freeSlot la rend `Init`, alors que freeSlot ne change pas l'état du noyau.
3. **W2** : avec l'exemption du §63.4, le cas ne peut plus exprimer le déplacement d'une ligne par un autre acteur pendant la vue.
4. **H49** : la règle de suite de Q9 rend `reject` les endUse 2 et 3, qui étaient `ok` dans la base historique de Q21.
5. **DS2-4** : la lecture retenue n'est pas plus stricte que l'alternative B de DS-R1 ; les deux sont incomparables.
6. **MM23-H16** : la règle de l'adresse la plus basse reste une décision du brief, pas une règle de la spec.

Je n'ai pas relancé l'audit final à plusieurs agents qui avait été interrompu. Les revues adverses faites à chaque phase, mes propres vérifications et la revue Codex de la PR le remplacent. La PR n'a pas de CI pour l'instant, et l'auto-fix est actif.

**Cause :** l'étape d'audit d'axiomes de `lean-action` importe le module racine `Ern`. Ce fichier ne contenait que des commentaires, donc l'audit n'a contrôlé aucune déclaration (« audited 0 declarations under 'Ern' ») et a échoué. Ce n'était pas lié à la PR : `main` échoue de la même façon depuis le commit de squelette.

**Correctif :** `formal/Ern.lean` importe maintenant les 25 modules. Le build local passe, racine comprise, sans avertissement.

Je n'ai pas lancé l'outil d'audit de la CI en local, car il faudrait télécharger un dépôt externe. Mon propre contrôle sur les mêmes 25 modules est plus strict (seuls `propext` et `Quot.sound` sont admis) et il passe. Si la CI échoue encore, l'auto-fix enverra un nouvel événement.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.
